tagline: Delivering reliable natural gas infrastructure for the clean energy economy
hero_kpi_rationale: Natural gas transported is a key indicator of WMB's operational activity, reflecting demand and utilization of its interstate transmission pipeline capacity.

kpis.name: Natural Gas Transported
kpis.explanation: Average annual volume of natural gas transported through WMB's pipelines
kpis.description: Gas transported is a key indicator of WMB's activity
kpis.signal: Decline in demand for transported natural gas

kpis.name: Natural Gas Liquids Sold
kpis.explanation: Average annual volume of natural gas liquids sold by WMB
kpis.description: NGLs are natural gas derivative products extracted during processing
kpis.signal: Increase in natural gas liquids sales

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: Gross margin is not a relevant metric for WMB as the majority of revenues come from regulated capacity fees, not cost of goods sold

kpis.name: Investments in LNG and Green Pipelines Infrastructure
kpis.explanation: Williams' initial investment in Louisiana LNG (10% stake) and Driftwood Pipeline (80%)
kpis.description: In October 2025, Williams invested $378 million to acquire a 10% stake in Louisiana LNG (export facility fully permitted) and an 80% stake in Driftwood Pipeline (greenfield Line 200). Both investments require additional capital for construction.
kpis.signal: Strategic investment in energy transition infrastructure

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

risks.title: Dependence on FERC Regulatory Approvals
risks.score_rationale: Several key projects (Transco Gulf Gillis, Southeast Supply Enhancement, Northeast Supply Enhancement) depend on FERC approvals, with recurring conditional language such as 'assuming timely receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals'. Delays or denials could block strategic revenue growth.

risks.title: Loss of Regulated Accounting Treatment
risks.score_rationale: The document states that if Transco or NWP lose regulated status, regulatory assets and liabilities would be reclassified, directly impacting financial results. Strong language regarding immediate financial consequences.

risks.title: Commodity Derivatives Volatility
risks.score_rationale: The Gas NGL Marketing Services segment exposes WMB to fair value accounting for commodity derivatives, generating significant volatility in unrealized gains and losses.

risks.title: Risk of Non-Recovery of Regulated Costs
risks.score_rationale: Recognition of regulatory assets depends on the anticipated probability of tariff recovery, a judgment subject to changes in regulatory policy or litigation.

risks.title: Dependence on Expansion Projects for Growth
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth in 2025 is driven by expansion projects placed in service (Deepwater Whale, Deepwater Shenandoah, Texas to Louisiana Energy Pathway). Future major projects (Gulf Gillis, Southeast Supply Enhancement) extend into 2027, with concentration and delay risks.

risks.title: Volume Risk on MVC Contracts
risks.score_rationale: The text notes a decline in MVC (Minimum Volume Commitments) revenues in certain segments, indicating exposure to customers not committing to future volumes.

risks.title: Operational Risk on Greenfield Projects
risks.score_rationale: Greenfield projects such as Driftwood Pipeline (Line 200) carry typical construction risks: cost overruns, execution delays, and technical complexity.

ai_positioning.summary: WMB does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 2025 Form 10-K filing.
